translation_direction: de → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete German electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Nathanael’s breathless, dash-broken letters, Clara’s calm reply and the narrator’s irony are kept distinct; the exclamation-heavy Romantic register is not toned down.
decisions.rationale: The story’s unease depends on the split between hysterical and rational voices.

decisions.decision: Konjunktiv II and conditional constructions are rendered with modal particles (hẳn, giá mà) so that ‘would have’ is not turned into ‘did’.
decisions.rationale: A reviewer found one such inversion in the first draft.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Er hätte ihn erwürgt’ (he would have strangled him) was rendered as a completed act; now ‘Anh hẳn đã bóp chết ông’ with the modal kept.
‘các người’ register slips, the dropped ‘thấu kính’, and a garbled clause in the first letter were corrected.
Nathanael’s tôi/anh/em pronouns, the term for the automaton and the ‘tẹp’ dialect marks were unified.
Typos and an ambiguous ‘anh ta’ were fixed.
‘hinter denen’ no longer read as ‘sau đó’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Ông Cát (Der Sandmann) at first use, then Ông Cát
glossary.rationale: The nursery bogeyman who throws sand in children’s eyes; the German name is kept once.

glossary.draft_rendering: người bán phong vũ biểu và thấu kính / ống nhòm bỏ túi
glossary.rationale: Coppola’s wares carry the eye imagery; one rendering throughout.
The automaton Olimpia is a ‘người máy’; the wooden doll is its taunt.

glossary.draft_rendering: tôi/cậu between Nathanael and Lothar; anh/em between Nathanael and Clara
glossary.rationale: One address system through the letters and the narrated scenes.

witness_decision: Selected the story ‘Der Sandmann’ from Project Gutenberg #6341, a transcription of E. T. A. Hoffmann’s Nachtstücke (Berlin: Realschulbuchhandlung, 1816–17). The edition that the Gutenberg text follows is not stated on the page and was not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: A few long periodic sentences remain heavier than German’s rhythm requires.

title_review.rationale: Der Sandmann is rendered ‘Ông Cát’ in the text; the Vietnamese edition title keeps the German name beside it.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: Nathanael’s letter about the barometer seller.
The ending: the narrator’s account of Clara.
